question_text: If the coefficients of the (2r + 4)-th term and the (3r + 4)-th term in the expansion of (1 + x)²¹ are equal, then find r.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find r — the coefficient of the k-th term, the rule for when two binomial coefficients are equal, and the value of r.
insider_note: Equal coefficients ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₛ has two branches, r = s and r + s = n. The first gives only the same term twice — the real answer comes from the r + s = 21 branch, the one students forget.

steps.label: Write the two coefficients and the rule
steps.margin_note: First mark. The k-th term of (1 + x)²¹ has coefficient ²¹Cₖ₋₁, so the two coefficients are ²¹C₂ᵣ₊₃ and ²¹C₃ᵣ₊₃. Two coefficients ⁿCᵣ, ⁿCₛ are equal when r = s or r + s = n.
steps.memory_tip: The k-th term of (1 + x)²¹ has coefficient ²¹Cₖ₋₁. Equal coefficients means r = s OR r + s = 21.
lines: The coefficient of the k-th term
ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₛ ⇒ r = s or r + s = n

recall.must_convey: That the coefficients are ²¹C₂ᵣ₊₃ and ²¹C₃ᵣ₊₃, and two binomial coefficients with the same n are equal when the lower indices are equal or add to n.
accept: the coefficients are twenty one C two r plus three and twenty one C three r plus three, and equal coefficients mean the indices are equal or add to twenty one
the k th term has coefficient n C k minus one
n C r equals n C s means r equals s or r plus s equals n
two r plus three and three r plus three equal or sum twenty one
use the rule that equal coefficients have indices adding to n

steps.why: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ is the only way two different binomial coefficients of the same n can be equal, so the rule has exactly two branches.
common_mistakes: Using ²¹C₂ᵣ₊₄ and ²¹C₃ᵣ₊₄ — the index is one less than the position.
Forgetting the r + s = n branch.

steps.label: Solve for r
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The first branch gives r = 0, which makes the two terms the same term; the second branch gives r = 3.
steps.memory_tip: The equal branch gives r = 0, the same term twice. The sum branch gives the real answer, r = 3.

recall.must_convey: That the equal-indices branch gives r = 0 (the same term twice) and the indices-add-to-21 branch gives r = 3.
accept: equal indices give r zero which is the same term, indices adding to twenty one give five r equals fifteen so r is three
two r plus three plus three r plus three is twenty one so r is three
indices add chesi twenty one pettithe r three vasthundi

steps.why: The branch r = 0 is not wrong, but it names one term twice; the question asks for the r that makes two DIFFERENT terms equal.
common_mistakes: Adding the indices as 5r + 6 = 21 and getting r = 3, then writing 5r = 21.
